d: Lonely, but lonely grove of laurels and cypresses that, with thinned art, encloses in a small plane the tomb of Eurydice. At the rising of the tent to the sound of a half symphony, the scene is seen occupied by a matte of Shepherds and Nymphaic followers of Orpheus who bring evenings of flowers and myrtle garlands; and while a part of them burns of the perfumes crowns the marble and scatters flowers around the tomb, the other the following Chorus, interrupted by the laments of Orpheus who, lying on the front of a stone, goes from time to time passionately replicating the name of Eurydice.
Horrid and cavernous beyond the Cocito River, then obscured in the distance by a dark smoke illuminated by flames that bulk up all that horrible dwelling.

Delicious for the green groves, the flowers that cover the meadows, the shady retreats that are discovered there, the rivers and streams that bathe it. Orpheus and the choir of Heroes and Heroes, then Eurydice.
Dark cave, forming a winding labyrinth, cluttered with boulders detached from the cliffs, which are all covered with dung and wild plants. Orpheus and Eurydice.
